candidates.description: Adaptation of the SoVI index of social vulnerability for Norwegian municipalities, modifying variables and conceptualizations for the Norwegian context
candidates.citation_sentence: In this article, we first replicate and then adapt an existing index of social vulnerability to hazard developed for the United States to a non-U.S. context.
candidates.notes: The adapted index produces valid results with Moran's autocorrelation of 0.374 (p=0.001) and is marginally better correlated with the Index for Living Conditions (r=0.49) than the replica (r=0.44). Authors present the adaptation as a successful contextualization. Paper uses numbered references [16] rather than author-date citations in body text; no DOI provided for the original Cutter et al. (2003) study in the paper; the adapted index is presented as marginally better but not explicitly validated as a clear success; the correlation between replica and adapted indexes is moderate (r=0.44) and the replica explains only 19% of variation in the adapted index.

candidates.description: Replication of the SoVI index of social vulnerability for Norwegian municipalities following the original US county-level methodology as closely as possible
candidates.citation_sentence: Our SoVI Replica analysis follows the original SoVI [16] as closely as possible regarding conceptualization of factors and the indicators included in the model.
candidates.notes: Paper uses numbered references [16] rather than author-date citations in body text; no DOI provided for the original Cutter et al. (2003) study in the paper; the moderate correlation (r=0.44) and low R-squared (0.19) leave the replication outcome genuinely ambiguous, with authors concluding adaptation is needed rather than explicitly calling the replication a failure or success.
